findings.description: Critical: the Force scenario remains unimplemented in the host procedure for non-empty backlogs. `SKILL.md` says `--force` reuses complete same-fingerprint caches without analyst dispatch, and `rank_candidates(..., scores=None)` now supports that via `_valid_prior_digest_for_reuse`, but Rank still instructs: when `requested_keys` is non-empty, dispatch exactly one analyst and always invoke `rank --scores`. Only the zero-candidate branch calls rank without scores. A host following the written Rank sequence on `/supervise cycle --force` over an unchanged non-empty store therefore re-dispatches and republishes a new `generated_at`, violating specs/supervise/spec.md scenario "Force does not discard valid scores".
findings.resolution: Extend Rank (and TestWorkflowContract) with an explicit force/same-fingerprint reuse branch: after prepare-batch, if fingerprint and requested keys match the prior digest and caches validate, call `rank` without `--scores` and skip analyst dispatch; dispatch only when reuse fails because scores are missing or composition changed.

findings.description: Nit: terminal decision history makes same-key re-admission unscorable and self-deleting. After reject/approve → prune, `_merge_terminal_history` keeps the terminal entry in the mirror; a later `store` of the same stub_key succeeds and reports `fresh_keys`, but `prepare_batch` skips any key whose decision is approved/rejected, yielding `requested_keys: []`. The next `store --prune-only` then deletes the freshly stored file again because the terminal decision still applies. Independently reproduced: re-admit → requested_keys=[] → second prune removes the candidate. Dedupe/seen_keys often masks this on the happy path, but any bypass (ledger reset, direct store, tests) permanently loses reconsidered work while consuming capacity.
findings.resolution: When `store` admits a key that only exists as terminal history, clear or supersede that terminal decision to pending for the new payload (or refuse re-admission explicitly). Add a regression covering reject → prune → re-store → prepare-batch → rank.

findings.description: Nit: `_valid_prior_digest_for_reuse` raises on a missing/mismatched singleton cache even when fingerprint and requested keys match the prior digest. Design D6 says force/reuse should dispatch for missing scores; raising aborts the scores=None path before the host can fall back to analyst dispatch. Independently reproduced by deleting one cache after a successful rank and calling `rank_candidates(..., scores=None)` with a later as_of.
findings.resolution: Return None (soft miss) from `_valid_prior_digest_for_reuse` when any required cache is absent or identity-invalid, and surface a distinct "scores required" error only after documenting the host fallback; alternatively add an explicit `--reuse-only` vs `--allow-rescore` mode.

findings.description: FYI: local installed copies under `.agents/skills/supervise/scripts/` and `.claude/skills/supervise/scripts/` still lack the d9c7f0a4 recovery/reuse/binding/UTC/pathspec fixes (`cmp` differs from `skills/supervise/scripts/digest.py` and `cycle_state.py`). SKILL.md mirrors are current. These paths are gitignored install outputs, so this is workspace hygiene rather than committed drift; harnesses that execute the installed copy would not see the round-1 fixes until `skills/install.sh` is re-run.
findings.resolution: Re-run `bash skills/install.sh` (or equivalent sync) before exercising supervise from `.agents`/`.claude` in this worktree.

findings.description: none: round-1 blockers verified fixed in runtime and tests: unscored lifecycle survivors prune without raising; force reuse works when rank is called without scores; recovery recovers then demands rehydrate; prepare/rank normalize due deferrals from stale records; rank binds manifests byte-for-byte to the persisted store including the empty-store case; staleness uses UTC dates with max(0,…); git evidence uses `:(literal)` pathspecs; legacy digested stubs canonicalize into schema-writable mirror entries; zero-candidate rank publishes a valid empty digest.
